set_aside.subject: K-02 repeatability qualification
set_aside.text: “Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself … is a promise about code that obtains neither.” The text also says obtaining time or chance by another route “is not detected.”
set_aside.question: What actor or kernel action establishes, with an observable output or failure, whether an implementation obtains time or chance and therefore whether the repeatability, repaired-slot and lasting-verdict promises apply?
options: The kernel records no qualification and these guarantees are only undocumented assumptions about the code
The author declares the qualification and the kernel stores it
Admission tests repeatability and records whether the qualification holds
The sandbox detects or blocks every source that counts as time or chance
set_aside.default_guess: Record no qualification and admit the implementation solely from its observed trial outputs, because the preceding sentence explicitly says other routes are not detected.

witness.initial: A contract version has a nonempty trial corpus, and an implementation can derive a changing value from a source other than the standard clock or randomness entry points while still sometimes producing the expected trial output.
events: The kernel executes the corpus and observes the expected output on that execution.
The kernel must decide whether to admit it and whether its recorded verdict carries the repeatability promises.
outcomes: One implementer admits it like any other implementation and provides no observable indication that the repeatability promises do not apply.
Another implementer adds an attestation or repeatability check and refuses it, or records that the promises do not apply.
witness.observer: The agent or owner sees admission with an apparently durable verdict versus refusal or a qualified verdict.
